finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the /hooks/test route on the `pub` router POSTs to an arbitrary caller-supplied URL with no validation. An attacker can reach internal services or cloud metadata endpoints, and the response status is returned as an oracle.

trace.note: pub.post('/hooks/test') handler; no auth middleware on the pub router (requireAdmin is applied only to the admin router at line 12)
req.body.callback is passed directly to axios.post; axios follows redirects by default
upstream status code is returned to the caller, which gives a port and host scanning oracle

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host or IP allowlist, no private-range or metadata-address block, no DNS resolution check, and no redirect limit. The only control in the file is requireAdmin, and it covers the admin router only. I could not see where `pub` is mounted, because routes.js is the only file in the directory, so any auth added at mount time is unverified. Not reported: admin GET /diagnostics/fetch (routes.js:15) also takes an unvalidated URL, but requireAdmin (routes.js:12) enforces admin, and an admin-run fetch diagnostic is treated as equal privilege.

verdict.reason: routes.js:19-21 passes req.body.callback straight into axios.post and returns r.status with no auth or URL validation on the pub router (requireAdmin at routes.js:12 covers only admin), though the mount point of pub is not visible, so any auth applied at mount time is unverified.
